Thanks for the quick intro earlier this week. We're kicking off a vendor evaluation for hosted inference and I wanted a straightforward snapshot of your standard IO pricing so we can model costs for a pilot. High level:
- Expected starting volume: ~10M tokens/month, ramp to ~50M over 3–6 months if results look good.
- Workload mix: ~60% chat-style (short prompts, longer outputs for summaries), ~30% classification/QA, ~10% embeddings for retrieval.

Could you send your standard per-1M token rates (input / output) for hosted API and a short list of the supported models you recommend for each workload class (chat/llm-summary, short-response, embeddings)? Also: do you publish any baseline latency profiles or token limits for each model?

Finally: are there standard volume-discount tiers or committed-usage pricing we should model? We're not yet ready to negotiate discounts but want to see the baseline and the thresholds.

If it's easier, a one-pager attachment with the rate card + model list is perfect.

Thanks —

Hi Carrie — thanks for the note and the context. Attached are two files: a compact rate card and a CSV snapshot of the model catalog tuned for common workloads. Quick summary (hosted API, list prices):

- Embeddings (embed-basic): $2.00 / 1M tokens (embeddings billed per input tokens only)
- Small / low-latency models (s-1): $4.00 / 1M input tokens | $4.00 / 1M output tokens
- Standard conversational models (c-1): $3.50 / 1M input tokens | $7.00 / 1M output tokens
- Long-context / high-quality (l-1): $6.00 / 1M input tokens | $12.00 / 1M output tokens

Notes:
- We separate input and output for clarity; streaming responses still count toward output tokens as they are generated.
- Model recommendations: for your chat/summary workload we typically recommend c-1 for most use cases and l-1 for longer clinical summaries or higher-quality synthesis. For embeddings use embed-basic. The attached CSV lists token limits and typical 95th-percentile response latencies for each model on our hosted tier.
- Baseline quotas: default per-account rate limits are in the attachment but we can adjust for pilots.

Volume discounts (standard published tiers):
- 50M+ tokens / month: 10% off list
- 200M+ tokens / month: 20% off list
- Commit-based custom pricing: available for annual/quarterly reserved capacity (we can provide worked examples).

If you can share a rough IO split (input vs output) and embedding volumes, I can send an example cost model (monthly) and a sample POC credit offer. Happy to hop on a quick call if you prefer—Karthik and I can join.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Hi Carrie — great questions, answers below plus a small worked example attached (NMB-example-pricing-commits.xlsx):

1) Typical chat IO ratio: for summary/clinical-note generation we often see output tokens in the 1.5x–2.5x range vs input, depending on prompt framing (short bullet prompts -> longer structured summaries). For conservative modeling use 2.0x output-to-input for summary-heavy flows.
2) Embeddings billing: correct — embeddings are billed on input tokens only; there are no output token charges for the embed endpoint.
3) Volume tiers: published discounts are aggregated across the account (all hosted-model usage combined). We apply the tier to aggregated monthly consumption; if you prefer model-specific commitments we can propose a reserved capacity example under Dedicated.

Worked example (baseline list prices, no discounts):
- 10M tokens / month, assumed split: 60% input (6M), 40% output (4M); assume chat uses c-1: cost = (6M * $3.50/1M) + (4M * $7.00/1M) = $21 + $28 = $49 / month (list)
- 50M tokens / month, same split: cost = (30M * $3.50/1M) + (20M * $7.00/1M) = $105 + $140 = $245 / month (list)

Applying the 50M+ tier (10% discount) example: 50M monthly becomes $220.50 / month. We can run a more exact model if you give us the expected embedding volumes and any long-context usage (l-1).

I'll drop the example spreadsheet and a labeled copy of the rate card into a shared HubSpot file and follow up in an hour with a suggested 30-minute time slot if you want to review.

Best,
Jasmine
